common.preconditionHint: Write one sentence per line that is clearly true or false. Refer to another todo as #id, and if a command verifies it, put 'Check: <command>' on the next line. An #id condition clears itself once that todo is done. A single sentence the code cannot judge keeps the todo out of autorun.
common.preconditionExample:
#57 must be done
Check: git -C ~/work/work-dashboard status --short

gtasks.title: Google Tasks sync
gtasks.toggleHint: Keeps your phone's Google Tasks in sync both ways
gtasks.intro: Connect Google Tasks to manage which categories are synced here.
gtasks.authStep2: Under APIs & Services → Library, enable the Google Tasks API.
gtasks.authStep3: Go to Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID.
gtasks.authStep4: Choose Desktop app as the application type.
gtasks.authStep5: Copy the client ID and client secret that are generated.
gtasks.formNote: Saved to ~/.claude/work-dashboard/gtasks.json, readable only by you. The Google consent screen opens next.
gtasks.planRule: Only what you choose is created on both sides and synced. Anything you skip is created nowhere.
gtasks.planBoth: On both sides — turning this on merges the two sets
gtasks.planOnlyLocal: Dashboard only — creates a list in Google
gtasks.planOnlyRemote: Google only — creates a category in the dashboard
gtasks.confirmDisconnect: This unlinks your Google account. Tasks on both sides stay as they are, and syncing resumes if you reconnect.
error.gtasksNeedConnect: Use the Connect button below to link Google Tasks first

report.hint.action: Done closes this task and tells the session that left it, if that session is running. Progress is passed on and the task stays open.

report.hint.confirm: Confirm marks it finally done. Sending a fix reopens it and passes the fix to the session that did the work — if that session is gone, the manager asks whether to start a helper to continue.

report.fixNoSessionNote: No session to continue, so the manager will ask whether to start a helper.

helper.hint: Sending passes it to this helper session. Task status does not change.

helper.ended: This helper session has already ended, so feedback is not sent.
permission.title: Permission requests
permission.unverified: Allow is blocked because the matching command was not found in the session log. Below is the manager's preview, with secrets masked and cut at 200 characters — deny it or answer in the session terminal.
permission.deadline: If not answered by {at}, it moves to the session's terminal prompt and can no longer be answered here.
permission.sentAllow: Allow sent — the session will run this command.
permission.sentDeny: Deny sent — the session continues without this command.
permission.terminalNote: The manager hook handed this request to the session's terminal prompt, so it cannot be answered here. Attach to the session in a terminal with the command below and answer there.
permission.endedNote: The session ended, so this permission prompt is gone too. To retry the work, send a resume instruction from the Session tab input — a new permission request will appear then.
